title: CS109 oral question bank
subject: CS109 oral question bank
system_prompt: You are an oral exam proctor for a university course.

questions.text: What is the definition of conditional probability?
rubric_items: Full credit: Clear and precise definition of conditional probability.
Partial credit: Mention of probability but lacks clarity on the conditional aspect.
Common mistakes: Confusing conditional probability with joint probability.

questions.text: Given that the probability of each baby showing up is 5/6, calculate the probability that exactly 5 babies show up out of 6 enrolled babies.
rubric_items: Full credit: Correct application of the binomial formula and accurate calculation.
Partial credit: Correct setup of the formula but incorrect calculation.
Common mistakes: Using the wrong values for n, k, or p in the formula.

questions.text: What is the probability that exactly 5 or 6 babies show up if the individual show-up probabilities for the 6 enrolled babies are p1, p2, ..., p6?
rubric_items: Full credit: Correctly identifies the expression for P(5) and P(6) using binomial coefficients.
Partial credit: Identifies the concept of independent probabilities but does not correctly express the probabilities.
Common mistakes: Confusing the probabilities with non-independent events or miscalculating the binomial coefficients.

questions.text: Under the normal assumption H1, what is P(0.9 < X < 1.0) if X is distributed as Normal(µ = 0.7, s² = 0.22)?
rubric_items: Full credit: Correctly calculates the z-scores and uses the standard normal table to find the correct probabilities.
Partial credit: Calculates z-scores but makes errors in looking up probabilities or interpreting the results.
Common mistakes: Forgetting to standardize the values or misapplying the normal distribution properties.

questions.text: What is the logit function and how does it relate to the Logit Normal distribution?
rubric_items: Full credit: Correctly defines the logit function and its role in the Logit Normal distribution.
Partial credit: Mentions the logit function but lacks clarity on its application.
Common mistakes: Confusing the logit function with other transformations or distributions.

questions.text: Under the normal assumption H1, calculate P(0.9 < X < 1.0) given that X follows Normal(µ = 0.7, s² = 0.22).
rubric_items: Full credit: Correctly calculates the Z-scores and finds the corresponding probabilities.
Partial credit: Attempts to standardize but makes arithmetic errors.
Common mistakes: Forgetting to standardize or using incorrect values for µ and s².
